headline: Harmonized archive metadata and semantic search make public sequencing data findable and reusable
label: Public Omics Metadata Harmonization
summary: Three tools released in November 2026 target the bottleneck of locating and reprocessing public omics data across SRA, GEO and INSDC/CNCB archives.
synthesis: The dominant thread is converting heterogeneous public archive records into queryable, comparable resources. SRAscout harmonizes SRA run and BioProject metadata for about 714,000 projects and adds BioBERT-embedding semantic search with filtering. MetaHQ consolidates standardized annotations from 13 curation sources for over 567k GEO samples and 27k studies, queried through a Python CLI. Meta2Data extends harmonization to processing, retrieving and standardizing microbiome data from INSDC and CNCB and running DADA2 or VSEARCH. New here is embedding-based semantic discovery on top of harmonized metadata, alongside cross-archive reprocessing. The tRNAdb 2026 update is a curated sequence-reference compilation and sits apart from this thread.
